observations: Photo 0 shows a Yamaha keyboard with 61 keys, black and cream-colored, placed on a wooden surface. The control panel is blue and black with a digital display, buttons, and a central dial with a numeric keypad.

Photo 1 is a close-up of the control panel, showing the same Yamaha branding and model number 'DSX-5599S' on the lower right. The display is off, and the keys are visible on the left. The control panel includes buttons for 'POWER/ON/OFF', 'SING/START/FILL/IN', 'START/STOP', 'MINUS/ONE', and a 'VOICE' button.
The keyboard appears to be a portable electronic keyboard with a built-in display and control panel. The keys show some wear and smudges, especially on the cream-colored keys.
The seller claims 'Original Yamaha tones, 100 voices & rhythm styles, headphone output & direct UK-Used Grade A'.

claims.claim: Original Yamaha tones, 100 voices & rhythm styles
claims.evidence: The model DSX-5599S is known to have 100 voices and rhythm styles, but the seller's claim is not directly verifiable from the photos. The display is off, and no audio or interface is shown to confirm functionality.
No headphone jack or output port is visible in either photo. The seller's claim cannot be confirmed remotely.
No proof of origin or condition is visible. The keyboard shows signs of use (smudges, wear), but no damage or wear is clearly visible to confirm 'Grade A'.

risks.risk: Keyboard may not power on or function properly
risks.proof: A video showing the keyboard turning on, displaying a menu, and playing a note.
A photo or video showing the headphone jack or output port, and a test of headphones connected to the device.

risks.risk: Model may be counterfeit or rebranded
risks.proof: A close-up of the serial number or a photo of the original packaging or warranty card.

risks.risk: Keys may be damaged or unresponsive
risks.proof: A video showing all keys being pressed and responding correctly.
risks.if_unproven: priced as keys may be faulty

proof_requests: Video of the keyboard powering on and playing a note.
Photo or video showing the headphone output port and test with headphones.
Close-up of the serial number or original packaging.
Video showing all keys being pressed and responding.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
